Translate the accepted NL0 into a small, usable Lean interface and local
proof plan. Start with source-map.json and the problem/specification; read
individual NL0 definitions or paragraphs when needed. Yui translation rules
are available on demand. Do not read every rule or background note at startup.
The controller retains all accepted paragraphs and attaches each step's own
Audit A note index. Notes are optional implementation references, not new
premise ports: do not give every note a Lean type or add it to premise_types.
Mathematically reviewed background notes are mathematical assessments, not already verified Lean
declarations. Resolve concrete library bindings and auxiliary proof details
in this phase. Prepare public interfaces and genuinely shared definitions;
leave per-node tactic choices and local lemma searches to proof workers.
Do not front-load a complete Mathlib-use inventory into serial preparation.
Keep the original H/E project inputs and every N/P output. The pinned Mathlib
environment is freely available without registration. Prefer direct library use
to M premise ports; omit M roots unless an intermediate port is useful. Choose a
coherent Lean representation preserving domains, assumptions, quantifiers and
the full target. Definitions cannot hide unproved results or stronger assumptions.
Inspect the actual pinned declarations and the meanings of order/index and
capability parameters, including overloaded notation and coercions. Explain
their source meaning rather than relying on remembered symbol conventions.
Use typed steps for mathematical obligations; no proof bodies are required yet.
Every complete node declaration must elaborate in its actual parameter and
direct-input context. Explicitly supply named arguments that cannot be inferred
from those argument types. The strict machine check rejects unresolved holes;
proof bodies cannot fill holes in a preceding theorem declaration.
Use the existing explanation/statement fields to settle mathematical ambiguity:
domains, equality or convergence mode, uniformity dependencies and interchange
conditions when relevant. Do not create dozens of administrative nodes or embed
Lean tactic recipes in NL0. Routine implementation length is not a source gap.

Submit an object with header, parameters, premise_types, conclusion_type,
representation, objects, steps, terminal, source_outputs, endpoint_correspondence.
endpoint_correspondence maps exactly every E ID and P to
{mode:direct|equivalent, explanation:<concise mathematical account>}. Explain
why each external statement and the WHOLE target (parameters, quantifiers,
hypotheses, conclusion) has the original meaning. Direct translations need only
a short account. For equivalent encodings, state the identification and why it
works in both directions under the actual assumptions. Do not invent a second
Lean representation just to prove an unnecessary conversion. If the proof
actually crosses two Lean representations, plan a checked conversion. These
notes are author guidance for the independent pre-freeze semantic review, not approval. header starts with
"import Mathlib
" and contains only object definitions/notation/structures,
no axioms, proof declarations, placeholders or executable metaprogramming.
parameters: [{name,type,binder_kind?}], where binder_kind is explicit (default),
implicit or instance. premise_types maps every H/E root and any retained M
port to its Lean proposition. Mathlib references are not a permission list. source_outputs maps every N/P to a distinct step Tddd. steps:
[{id,statement,inputs:[root/T IDs],source_steps:[S IDs],explanation}]. Each step
is a closed conditional obligation; include useful independent subarguments or
representation bridges when they reduce work. Every step must reach terminal;
cover all source paragraphs. terminal's type equals conclusion_type. objects
may be [] when special representation views are unnecessary. representation
explains the chosen encoding; it is not a semantic approval.

Save incomplete work with save_interface_draft; revise it with base_candidate
and explicit JSON-pointer patches. Use check_lean_types for uncertain APIs or
small type fragments, and check_draft when the full interface is ready. A full
check runs real Lean type elaboration and source-boundary checks. Continue from
your saved candidate after errors. Do not stop just to report ordinary progress.
At author acceptance, a separate semantic interface reviewer checks source
correspondence before proof workers start. Final Audit B independently checks semantic
faithfulness and the assembled proof. A type check is never a semantic PASS.

Read the stage rules on demand; no need to preload the whole skill. Relevant frozen rule paths (relative to the installed skill root): nl02lean/references/minimal-translation.md. Other declared Markdown references linked from these remain available through read_yui. Reads return explicit pages of at most 250 lines with continuation metadata. Follow relevant links; operator scheduling/control manuals are not proof-worker inputs.
Frozen task document IDs: background-supplement.json, nl0.json, problem.md, source-map.json, spec.json, target-selection.json. Use read_task_input to read them.
Prefer check_draft/submit_draft with an actual artifact JSON object. The older check_artifact/submit_artifact wrappers require artifact_json to be a double-encoded valid JSON string; do not supply Python dictionaries or single-quoted keys. Both forms run identical checks.
You may revise an explicit pre-freeze prior-interface.json through {"base_input":"prior-interface.json","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"/header","value":"complete replacement header"}]}. The result is fully expanded and checked; this never supplies missing mathematics. After a full candidate exists, preserve it with base_candidate:N and explicit patches, or submit {"accept_candidate":N} only when that actual candidate is complete and faithful. read_interface_draft kind=index lists your own actual full candidates and partial type probes; kind=candidate reads a JSON pointer of a full candidate, kind=probe reads its own actual partial header/types. After context reset, inspect this index rather than starting from a vacuous True template. A placeholder is not a translation. Choose useful closed obligations; a large worker limit cannot accelerate a monolithic job. Optional shared_obligations must use the existing v2 schema and describe only existing NL0 lemmas or implementation extraction, with explicit inputs and route. They remain pending actual semantic review; new mathematics returns to NL0.

{"id": "source-map.json", "pointer": "", "view": "value", "value": {"background_mode": "node_local_reference", "source_steps": [{"id": "S001", "text": "Fix x∈ℝ^n and t>0. H001 gives positive finite dimensions and H002 permits all derivatives used here. By H004, u·u=1. Differentiation in time, by the ordinary product rule for the finite component sum defining the dot product, gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Choose the pointwise scalar a from H005. Then u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses no derivative or regularity of a."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Twice differentiating u·u=1 in time gives 2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt=0. For an arbitrary coordinate j0∈{1,...,n}, twice differentiating in x_{j0} similarly gives 2|∂_{x_{j0}}u|²+2u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=0. Thus u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=−|∂_{x_{j0}}u|². Generalize j0 over the spatial coordinates. Dot the normality equation for a with u and use |u|²=1. Finite distributivity and the definition of Δ_xu give a=u·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². The same calculation applies to every scalar satisfying that pointwise equation."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "F001 proves the two orthogonality identities at the arbitrary point. By F002 substitute the computed value of a into the pointwise normality equation from H005 to obtain u_tt−Δ_xu=(Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u. The scalar was chosen only at this point and is eliminated; it is not promoted to a regular scalar field. Generalizing x and t proves all the asserted pointwise identities."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Fix t0>0 and set J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Both endpoints are positive and the first is strictly smaller than the second. Apply H006 to these two times to obtain a compact set outside which u=q throughout J."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Choose such a compact C from F001. Compact subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded: for example the increasing family of open boxes with positive integral radii covers C, and a finite subcover puts C in one such box. Enlarging its radius if needed gives a positive radius with strict containment in the open box. This also covers C empty."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Choose R as in F002 and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. The complement of compact C is open. On the open set (ℝ^n∖C)×int J the map u is the constant q by F001. H002 implies that all positive-order derivatives vanish on that open set. Thus at interior times e, e_t and the products u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every j vanish outside C. Products and finite sums of smooth derivatives are continuous; in particular e and e_t are jointly continuous on the original open space-time domain."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "At any r∈int J, each spatial function in question is continuous, hence Lebesgue measurable, and bounded on compact Q. Its absolute value is bounded by a finite nonnegative constant times the indicator of Q, since it vanishes outside C⊂Q. The integral of that bound is the constant times (2R)^n, which is finite. This proves absolute integrability of e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every spatial index j. No interchange of a derivative and an integral is used here."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Since t0∈int J, F004 in particular proves integrability of e(·,t0). Generalize the arbitrary t0 and existentially retain the compatible C,R and their box Q, together with F001–F004, to obtain the full quantified support and integrability assertion. Joint continuity of e and e_t was established in S003 using H002. The energy integral has therefore been proved finite at every positive time, before introducing the finite energy function."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Fix t0>0 and take J,C,R,Q from N002 at this t0. The guarded definition E is now available. By H001 and H002, the finite product rule and equality of mixed spatial and time derivatives give, at all x and positive t, e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t). The products and e_t are integrable at every positive time by N002."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Set η=t0/4. Then η>0 and [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. Joint continuity of e_t from N002 on the compact set Q×[t0−η,t0+η] gives a finite nonnegative upper bound for |e_t| there. Indeed its continuous absolute value has a bounded compact image in ℝ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Choose B0 from F002. For arbitrary x and 0<|h|<η, apply M004 to the real function r↦e(x,r), with derivative r↦e_t(x,r), on the closed interval whose endpoints are min(t0,t0+h) and max(t0,t0+h). Smoothness gives continuity and the indicated derivative on that interval; all times lie in [t0−η,t0+η]. If a total function on ℝ is required, set it to zero at nonpositive times; this leaves this positive interval and its local derivatives unchanged. For x∈Q, M004 and F002 imply |(e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0))/h|≤B0. This is the same slope in either ordering of the endpoints. For x∉Q both densities vanish by N002, so the quotient is zero. Thus the uniform dominating function on ℝ^n is B0·1_Q, where 1_Q is one on Q and zero off Q. It is integrable since Q is measurable of finite measure."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Fix an arbitrary sequence hseq:ℕ→ℝ. Temporarily assume L1: for every k, 0<|hseq(k)|<η and hseq(k)→0. Define Fseq(k)(x)=[e(x,t0+hseq(k))−e(x,t0)]/hseq(k). Each Fseq(k) is continuous in x and hence almost everywhere strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure. F003 gives the bound |Fseq(k)(x)|≤B0·1_Q(x) for every k and x. The definition of the time derivative gives Fseq(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) at every x, because hseq tends to zero through nonzero increments. All Fseq(k) are integrable, by the bound or by integrability of their two densities."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Apply M001 with measurable space ℝ^n, Lebesgue measure, codomain ℝ, sequence Fseq, limit x↦e_t(x,t0), and bound B0·1_Q. F003 and F004 verify all premises. It follows that ∫Fseq(k) dx→∫e_t(x,t0) dx. Since both densities are integrable by N002, linearity of the real Lebesgue integral identifies the left integral with [E(t0+hseq(k))−E(t0)]/hseq(k)."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Discharge L1: F005 holds for every sequence of nonzero increments tending to zero and having absolute value less than η. This proves the full punctured limit as the increment tends to zero: otherwise one could choose, in successively smaller punctured neighborhoods of zero, increments whose energy quotients stay a fixed positive distance from ∫e_t(x,t0)dx. Such a sequence tends to zero and lies in that same increment range, contradicting F005. Thus E is differentiable at t0 with E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx. Together with F001, and generalization of arbitrary t0, this proves the full asserted differentiability formula and its integrability clauses. Neither the chosen support witnesses nor the test sequence escapes this conclusion."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Fix t0>0 and j∈{1,...,n}, and choose compatible J,C,R,Q from N002 at t0. Define g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0). It is smooth by H002. It is zero off C by N002. Since the compact C lies in int Q, there is a neighborhood of ∂Q disjoint from C (and if C is empty all these functions are zero everywhere). Therefore g vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The product rule gives ∂_{x_j}g=∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u+u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u at time t0. All three derivative integrands are integrable by N002."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Let Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1), and let T(y,z) insert z into coordinate j, keeping the other coordinates in their original order. Set Hfun(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g(T(y,z)). The coordinate permutation identifies Q with Qrest×[−R,R] and Lebesgue integration on Q with integration for the product of Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest and Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]. This follows from the Cartesian product definition of Euclidean Lebesgue measure: rectangles have the product of their side lengths, invariant under coordinate reordering; that determines this measure. If n=1 the remaining factor ℝ^0 is a singleton with mass one, so the same identification applies. Both restricted measures are finite, hence s-finite. Hfun is continuous and bounded on this compact product; the product measure is finite, so Hfun is integrable there. For each fixed y∈Qrest, z↦g(T(y,z)) is smooth with derivative Hfun(y,z). Its derivative is bounded on [−R,R], hence interval integrable, and its endpoint values are zero by F001."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "For arbitrary y∈Qrest apply M003 with codomain ℝ, endpoints −R,R, f(z)=g(T(y,z)), and derivative d(z)=Hfun(y,z). R>0 and F002 give the ordering, continuity, derivative and integrability premises. It follows that ∫_{−R}^{R}Hfun(y,z) dz=g(T(y,R))−g(T(y,−R))=0. Since endpoints have one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, the interval integral equals the integral for Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]. Generalize y."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Apply M002 to Hfun with outer measure Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest and inner measure Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R], codomain ℝ. F002 proves product integrability and s-finiteness. The iterated integral is zero by F003. Fubini therefore gives zero for the product integral, and the coordinate identification in F002 gives ∫_Q ∂_{x_j}g dx=0. This holds also in the singleton outer factor when n=1."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "By F001 the derivative and both product summands vanish outside Q, so their whole-space integrals equal their integrals over Q. Integrate the product identity in F001, using absolute integrability and linearity. F004 gives 0=∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u dx+∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx, at time t0. Symmetry of the Euclidean dot product gives the asserted identity with ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t on the left. Generalize t0 and j to obtain the asserted integration-by-parts identity, including the integrability clauses."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Fix t0>0. N002 proves integrability of e(·,t0) and of all product terms below, so E is the actual finite integral. N003 proves its differentiability and gives E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx with e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Substitute this identity, use linearity and interchange the finite sum and integral (H001 gives a finite dimension), and apply N004 to each j. This yields E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·u_tt dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu) dx, all fields evaluated at t0."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "By N001 the final integrand in F001 is zero at every x, so E'(t0)=0. Since t0 was arbitrary, N002 and N003 together prove the complete target: e(·,t) is integrable and E is differentiable with E'(t)=0 for every positive t. {"id": "problem.md", "total_lines": 167, "start": 1, "end": 167, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 29, "requested_end": 200, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.

457: /-! ### Smooth functions within a set -/
458: 
459: variable (𝕜) in
460: /-- A function is continuously differentiable up to `n` on `s` if, for any point `x` in `s`, it
461: admits continuous derivatives up to order `n` on a neighborhood of `x` in `s`.
462: The parameter `n` belongs to `ℕ∞ω` (accessible in the `ContDiff` scope), i.e. it can be a natural
463: number, `∞`, or `ω`.
464: 
465: For `n = ∞`, we only require that this holds up to any finite order (where the neighborhood may
466: depend on the finite order we consider).
467: For `n = ω`, we require the function to be analytic within `s` at every point of `s`. The precise
468: definition we give (all the derivatives should be analytic) is more involved to work around issues
469: when the space is not complete, but it is equivalent when the space is complete.
470: -/
471: @[fun_prop]
472: def ContDiffOn (n : ℕ∞ω) (f : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop :=
473:   ∀ x ∈ s, ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x
474: 
475: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.contDiffOn {n : ℕ∞} {f' : E → FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F}
476:     (hf : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f f' s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s := by
477:   intro x hx m hm
478:   use s
479:   simp only [Set.insert_eq_of_mem hx, self_mem_nhdsWithin, true_and]
480:   exact ⟨f', hf.of_le (mod_cast hm)⟩
481: 
482: theorem ContDiffOn.contDiffWithinAt (h : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s) (hx : x ∈ s) :
483:     ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x :=
484:   h x hx
485: 
486: @[fun_prop]
487: theorem ContDiffOn.of_le (h : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s) (hmn : m ≤ n) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 m f s := fun x hx =>
488:   (h x hx).of_le hmn
489: 
490: theorem ContDiffWithinAt.contDiffOn' (hm : m ≤ n) (h' : m = ∞ → n = ω)
491:     (h : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x) :
492:     ∃ u, IsOpen u ∧ x ∈ u ∧ ContDiffOn 𝕜 m f (insert x s ∩ u) := by

const header=`import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

namespace WaveMap

abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev V (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => density u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dt (dt u) p)
noncomputable def mixedProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dx u j p) (dx (dt u) j p)
noncomputable def lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx (dx u j) j p)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx u j p)
noncomputable def fluxDx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => flux u j (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)

def sectionGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

def supportGeometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ slab t, u (x, r) = q) ∧
  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ (k + 1) u (x, r) = 0)

def supportSections {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    sectionGood C R (fun x => density u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => densityT u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => timeProduct u (x, r)) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n,
      sectionGood C R (fun x => mixedProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => lapProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => fluxDx u j (x, r)))

noncomputable def quotient {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ :=

abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev V (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => density u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dt (dt u) p)
noncomputable def mixedProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dx u j p) (dx (dt u) j p)
noncomputable def lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx (dx u j) j p)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx u j p)
noncomputable def fluxDx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => flux u j (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)

def sectionGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

def supportGeometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ slab t, u (x, r) = q) ∧
  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ (k + 1) u (x, r) = 0)

def supportSections {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    sectionGood C R (fun x => density u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => densityT u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => timeProduct u (x, r)) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n,
      sectionGood C R (fun x => mixedProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => lapProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => fluxDx u j (x, r)))

noncomputable def quotient {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ :=
  (density u (x, t + h) - density u (x, t)) / h

abbrev Other {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) := {i : Fin n // i ≠ j}
def insertCoord {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (y : Other j → ℝ) (z : ℝ) : X n :=
  fun i => if h : i = j then z else y ⟨i, h⟩
def otherBox {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (R : ℝ) : Set (Other j → ℝ) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)

end WaveMap

import Mathlib

    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :

noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :

  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dt (dt u) p)

  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

def supportGeometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ slab t, u (x, r) = q) ∧
  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧

    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    sectionGood C R (fun x => density u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => densityT u (x, r)) ∧

    (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ :=
  (density u (x, t + h) - density u (x, t)) / h

import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

namespace WaveMap

abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev V (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => density u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dt (dt u) p)
noncomputable def mixedProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dx u j p) (dx (dt u) j p)
noncomputable def lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx (dx u j) j p)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx u j p)
noncomputable def fluxDx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => flux u j (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)

def sectionGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

def supportGeometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ slab t, u (x, r) = q) ∧
  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ (k + 1) u (x, r) = 0)

def supportSections {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    sectionGood C R (fun x => density u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => densityT u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => timeProduct u (x, r)) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n,
      sectionGood C R (fun x => mixedProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => lapProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => fluxDx u j (x, r)))

noncomputable def quotient {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ :=
  (density u (x, t + h) - density u (x, t)) / h

abbrev Other {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) := {i : Fin n // i ≠ j}
def insertCoord {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (y : Other j → ℝ) (z : ℝ) : X n :=
  fun i => if h : i = j then z else y ⟨i, h⟩
def otherBox {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (R : ℝ) : Set (Other j → ℝ) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)

end WaveMap

premise_types.H004: ∀ x : WaveMap.X n, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ‖u (x, t)‖ = 1

import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

namespace WaveMap

abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ

def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => density u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :

noncomputable def mixedProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :

def sectionGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧

  (density u (x, t + h) - density u (x, t)) / h

  fun i => if h : i = j then z else y ⟨i, h⟩

artifact.header:
import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

namespace WaveMap

abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev V (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => density u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dt (dt u) p)
noncomputable def mixedProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dx u j p) (dx (dt u) j p)
noncomputable def lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx (dx u j) j p)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx u j p)
noncomputable def fluxDx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => flux u j (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)

def sectionGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

def supportGeometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ slab t, u (x, r) = q) ∧
  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ (k + 1) u (x, r) = 0)

def supportSections {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    sectionGood C R (fun x => density u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => densityT u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => timeProduct u (x, r)) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n,
      sectionGood C R (fun x => mixedProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => lapProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => fluxDx u j (x, r)))

noncomputable def quotient {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ :=
  (density u (x, t + h) - density u (x, t)) / h

abbrev Other {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) := {i : Fin n // i ≠ j}
def insertCoord {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (y : Other j → ℝ) (z : ℝ) : X n :=
  fun i => if h : i = j then z else y ⟨i, h⟩
def otherBox {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (R : ℝ) : Set (Other j → ℝ) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)

end WaveMap

On the open complement times the interior slab u is locally constant, so every positive-order joint derivative vanishes. This is support geometry only, without selecting any witness globally.

    WaveMap.supportGeometry u q t C R ∧ WaveMap.supportSections u t C R) ∧

steps.explanation: For each compatible support witness obtain continuity, vanishing, compact-box bounds and absolute integrability for exactly the six families in N002, by a constant times the box indicator. Include joint continuity of density and its time derivative on t>0 and integrability at every positive time. Existential witnesses stay together with their section properties. Exports N002; establishes the finite-energy guard.

steps.statement:
∀ x : WaveMap.X n, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
  HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => WaveMap.density u (x, r)) (WaveMap.densityT u (x, t)) t ∧
  WaveMap.densityT u (x, t) =
    2 * WaveMap.timeProduct u (x, t) + 2 * ∑ j : Fin n, WaveMap.mixedProduct u j (x, t)
steps.explanation: Apply the finite product rule and equality of mixed derivatives on the positive open domain. Supply an actual HasDerivAt assertion for density as well as the expanded derivative identity; this is the derivative used by the mean value theorem and pointwise quotient convergence.

steps.statement:

  0 < η ∧ 0 ≤ B ∧ 0 < R ∧ η < t ∧
  Integrable ((WaveMap.box n R).indicator (fun _ => B)) ∧
  ∀ h : ℝ, 0 < |h| → |h| < η → ∀ x : WaveMap.X n,
    |WaveMap.quotient u t h x| ≤ (WaveMap.box n R).indicator (fun _ => B) x
steps.explanation: At each fixed t choose η=t/4 and compatible C,R. Compactness of box × [t-η,t+η] bounds densityT by a nonnegative B depending on t and the support witnesses, uniformly in x and in the allowed increments. Use exists_hasDerivAt_eq_slope on the ordered endpoints, together with zero density off the box. The integrable dominating function is the displayed box indicator times B; η<t ensures all sampled times are positive.

steps.statement:

    HasDerivAt (WaveMap.energy u) (∫ x : WaveMap.X n, WaveMap.densityT u (x, t)) t ∧
    Integrable (fun x : WaveMap.X n => WaveMap.densityT u (x, t)) ∧
    Integrable (fun x : WaveMap.X n => WaveMap.timeProduct u (x, t)) ∧
    ∀ j : Fin n, Integrable (fun x : WaveMap.X n => WaveMap.mixedProduct u j (x, t))) ∧

Apply MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence with real codomain and Lebesgue volume. Linearity identifies the integral quotient with the energy quotient, using T004 at both positive times. Discharge the sequence assumptions and use the sequential criterion for the punctured real limit to get HasDerivAt of energy. Retain the density formula and integrability of every displayed term. This exports N003 without assuming an integral interchange.

steps.statement:

  IntegrableOn f (WaveMap.box n R) →

steps.explanation: Prove the coordinate integration bridge for the actual insertion map and restricted boxes, under the stated IntegrableOn premise. Use the finite-product measure-preserving split (MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piEquivPiSubtypeProd with predicate i ≠ j), evaluate its singleton complementary factor, and apply Fubini for the finite restricted measures. otherBox uses all coordinates except j in inherited order; when n=1 this is the singleton empty tuple with mass one. This is the checked conversion required by the coordinate FTC argument, not an assumption about arbitrary rearrangement of measures.

Endpoints have zero Lebesgue measure, identifying interval and closed-set integrals. Use T008, product integrability and MeasureTheory.integral_integral to conclude the box integral of fluxDx is zero, then its whole-space integral is zero by support. steps.explanation: Integrate the T009 product identity by linearity, using T004 for both product integrabilities, and rearrange the zero total derivative integral. The mixedProduct convention already places dx u first using symmetry of the real Euclidean inner product. Generalize t>0 and j. Exports all of N004.

steps.statement:
∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
  Integrable (fun x : WaveMap.X n => WaveMap.density u (x, t)) ∧
  DifferentiableAt ℝ (WaveMap.energy u) t ∧ deriv (WaveMap.energy u) t = 0
steps.explanation: Combine the differentiated integral identity and its expanded density with integration by parts in each finite coordinate. All terms are integrable by N002/N003/N004, allowing finite summation and integral linearity. Recombine the Laplacian and use the pointwise orthogonality of N001 to make the final integrand zero. Obtain differentiability and deriv energy = 0 at every t>0, retaining integrability.

steps.statement:
(∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
  Integrable (fun x : WaveMap.X n => WaveMap.density u (x, t)) ∧
  DifferentiableAt ℝ (WaveMap.energy u) t ∧ deriv (WaveMap.energy u) t = 0) ∧
  ∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < t → WaveMap.energy u s = WaveMap.energy u t
steps.explanation: Retain T011 and apply exists_hasDerivAt_eq_slope to energy on a positive interval with ordered endpoints. Differentiability gives continuity at the endpoints and zero derivative in the interior; slope zero gives equality of energies. Reverse endpoint order or handle equal times as needed. This is the complete P, including constancy, with no time-zero assertion.

P.explanation: Positive integer dimensions are represented by n,m : ℕ with H001 : 1≤n ∧ 1≤m, a bijective encoding. X n is the usual real Cartesian coordinate space with product Lebesgue measure; V m has exactly the Euclidean norm and dot product. Fin n reindexes all n coordinates without changing finite sums. H002 asserts joint C∞ smoothness on precisely t>0, using the inner infinity smoothness index; H003/H004 keep both unit conditions. H005 is the original pointwise existential scalar normality equation, with no scalar field regularity. H006 retains a single compact spatial set for every entire positive closed time interval. A source map on t>0 extends arbitrarily to the total u used here, and any such u restricts back; locality preserves all positive-time derivatives and hypotheses in both directions. dt, dx and lap give the componentwise time/spatial derivatives and Laplacian, and density is exactly the unhalved sum of their Euclidean squares. T004 proves the guard that makes energy the actual finite Lebesgue integral. The conclusion explicitly asserts absolute integrability, real differentiability and zero derivative at every positive time, together with energy equality for every pair of positive times. Restriction and extension therefore give the whole source target in both directions; no conclusion at nonpositive times or additional hypothesis is present.
